promise: Increase defence spending to 2.5% of GDP
description: Starmer announced on February 25, 2025 that defence spending would rise to 2.5% of GDP from April 2027, funded partly by reducing aid to 0.3% of GNI. The implementation date remains future.
evidence: Government announcement specifies April 2027; appropriations and plans are not proof of achieved expenditure.
Outcome not established as of 2026-09-21: the April 2027 implementation date remains future and the checked funding plan is not a spending outturn.

role: Prime Minister of the United Kingdom
promise: Raise defence spending to 2.5% of GDP from April 2027, with a conditional ambition of 3% in the next parliament
description: Starmer announced the 2.5% target on February 25, 2025. The government separately described a 2.6% total including intelligence and security expenditure; the measures must not be conflated.
evidence: The Spring Statement confirms April 2027 commencement and conditions on the longer-term ambition; fulfillment is not yet due.
